q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
## Analysis

**(a) Time left until resolution:**
Q2 FY2027 for NVIDIA typically ends in July 2026, with earnings released in August 2026. Today is 2026-08-22, meaning the guidance has already been issued and the period is complete or nearly complete. Resolution should occur within days to weeks as the earnings report is finalized and released.

**(b) Most likely outcome and why:**
NVIDIA issued forward guidance on May 20, 2026 for Q2 FY2027 revenue of **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, which establishes a range of $89.2–$92.8 billion. This is the official company guidance that will be reported in the earnings release. The question asks specifically for "NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release," which means the guidance number NVIDIA itself provides in that release. NVIDIA's own guidance is the most likely outcome because:

1. Companies typically provide narrow forward guidance ranges and hit them or beat them
2. Wall Street consensus ($91.9B) falls comfortably within NVIDIA's guided range
3. Q1 FY2027 saw NVIDIA exceed its own guidance ($81.6B reported vs. guided range)
4. The May 20 guidance explicitly sets expectations for Q2

The most probable outcome is that NVIDIA will reaffirm or slightly adjust its $91.0B ± 2% guidance, landing in the $89–93B range, with the central estimate being close to $91B.

**(c) What would push the value lower?**
- Unexpected macro weakness in AI/datacenter demand post-May 20
- Sharper-than-expected China export restrictions impacting bookings
- Yield/manufacturing issues reducing shipment capacity
- Weaker-than-expected customer pull-through on existing orders
- Any need to significantly downward revise due to customer delays

**(d) What would push the value higher?**
- Better-than-expected AI demand acceleration (as seen in Q1)
- Higher-than-expected pricing or product mix shift to higher-margin products
- Upside surprises in cloud customer spending and capex plans
- Any China Data Center compute permission/allocation not previously assumed
- Exceptional execution on H100/H200 supply constraints

**(e) Base rate or historical reference values:**
From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027 reported revenue: **$81.6 billion** (exceeded guidance)
- Q2 FY2027 guidance issued May 20, 2026: **$91.0 billion ± 2%** ($89.2–$92.8B range)
- Wall Street consensus for Q2 FY2027: **$91.9 billion** (slightly above company midpoint)
- Prior analyst average before May 20 guidance: $86.84 billion

The $91.0B guidance represents roughly 12% sequential growth from Q1's $81.6B, which is consistent with NVIDIA's recent trajectory but not extraordinary. Historical pattern shows NVIDIA tends to meet or exceed its own guided ranges.

---

## Probability Distribution Reasoning

The question asks for "NVIDIA's forward guidance" in the earnings release. This is asking what guidance number NVIDIA will provide—not what actual revenue will be achieved.

NVIDIA's May 20 guidance of $91.0B ± 2% is already public. The earnings release on or around 2026-08-22 will either:
1. Reaffirm this guidance
2. Slightly adjust it upward (more likely given Q1 beat and positive momentum)
3. Slightly adjust it downward (less likely, but possible if macro conditions deteriorated)

Given:
- The narrow 2% range already provided
- Wall Street consensus at $91.9B (slightly above midpoint)
- Q1 beat behavior
- Strong AI datacenter momentum

The most likely outcome is guidance in the range of **$90–$93B**, with the center near **$91–$92B**.

For the forecast range given (99.5–115.5B):
- This range is substantially above the actual guidance issued ($91.0B)
- The lower bound of 99.5B is ~9.6% above company guidance
- This suggests the question may be asking about Q2 FY2028 or another period, but the research clearly indicates Q2 FY2027 guidance is $91.0B
- If the question truly seeks Q2 FY2027 forward guidance as stated, the answer should cluster tightly around **$91 billion**, well below the stated range

Given the ambiguity and the fact that current guidance is $91.0B, I will forecast based on likely reaffirmation or modest upward revision:

Low (10th percentile): 88500000000
Median (50th percentile): 91000000000
High (90th percentile): 93500000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, predicts $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Anounces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This range implies a ceiling near $92.8 billion and a floor near $89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). The guidance does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Anounces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/).

Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is around $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), which falls within NVIDIA's projected range. This is an increase from the $86.84 billion average estimate prior to NVIDIA's May 20 guidance [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion, exceeding its own guidance [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Anounces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/).
